Aug 1, 2026 · 1 min read

Privacy and security awareness

Designing privacy into a prototype before adding features

The change made the project simpler.

Read the full note

While sketching a small browser-based prototype, I caught myself treating privacy as a settings screen I could add near the end. I restarted the plan by listing what data the idea truly needed, what could stay on the device, and what should never be collected.

The change made the project simpler. Privacy by design is not only about preventing harm; it can also force clearer decisions about what a product is actually for.

Jul 18, 2026 · 1 min read

Ethical technology use

Threat modeling is a technical form of empathy

Security thinking gets stronger when it includes the experience of the person using the system.

Read the full note

My first threat-modeling exercise felt like a list of things that could go wrong. It became more useful when I stopped thinking only about attackers and started asking who could be confused, excluded, pressured, or exposed by an ordinary design decision.

Security thinking gets stronger when it includes the experience of the person using the system. Anticipating misuse and anticipating friction are both ways of taking people seriously.

Jul 3, 2026 · 1 min read

Responsible online participation

Cleaning a repository is part of communicating responsibly

Good documentation respects other people's time.

Read the full note

A repository can technically work while still making the next person search through unclear names, generated files, and missing context. I treated a cleanup session as communication work: organize the structure, explain the purpose, and make the useful path obvious.

Good documentation respects other people's time. A clear project also makes it easier for me to notice what I actually understand and what I have only been carrying forward.

Jun 11, 2026 · 1 min read

Community contribution

Accessibility belongs inside digital citizenship

Accessibility is not an optional polish layer.

Read the full note

I reviewed a form using only a keyboard and quickly found places where the visual design looked finished but the interaction did not. Labels, focus order, contrast, and motion preferences determine who can actually participate.

Accessibility is not an optional polish layer. If digital citizenship is about contributing to spaces responsibly, access has to be part of the definition from the beginning.

accessibilityinclusive designkeyboard

May 22, 2026 · 1 min read

Media literacy

Checking the links behind a persuasive video

Production quality can make a claim feel verified before any verification happens.

Read the full note

A polished video used charts and confident narration to make its conclusion feel settled. I followed the sources in the description and found that one link did not support the number shown, while another was several years older than the narration implied.

Production quality can make a claim feel verified before any verification happens. I now treat confidence, editing, and visual polish as presentation signals—not evidence signals.

Reflection and self-improvement

Reviewing my digital footprint before the next school year

The goal was not to erase personality, but to make sure my digital footprint reflects the kind of learner and community member I want to be: curious, responsible, and increasingly aware of cybersecurity and digital citizenship.

Read the full note

As I look ahead to starting electrical engineering in Canada, I wanted to review what I am publicly attaching to my name online. That meant checking bios, old posts, shared profiles, and the tone of the spaces where I participate most.

The goal was not to erase personality, but to make sure my digital footprint reflects the kind of learner and community member I want to be: curious, responsible, and increasingly aware of cybersecurity and digital citizenship.

Cross-checking AI summaries before I trust them

That extra step slowed me down slightly, but it improved my confidence and made my notes more accurate.

Read the full note

AI summaries are useful for orientation, but they often compress uncertainty out of a topic. This week I started checking every summary against at least one primary source before I reuse any claim.

That extra step slowed me down slightly, but it improved my confidence and made my notes more accurate. Convenience is only ethical when it still leaves room for responsibility.

Cybersecurity feels more manageable when I break it into repeated habits instead of waiting for a problem to force a reaction.

Using AI for study support without outsourcing my thinking

I set a simple rule for myself: AI can help me start, compare, or check, but it should not replace the part where I explain the idea in my own words.

Read the full note

I experimented with using AI to organize study questions and explain unfamiliar terms, but I kept noticing how easy it was to let the tool become the voice of the work. That is useful for speed, but risky for learning.

I set a simple rule for myself: AI can help me start, compare, or check, but it should not replace the part where I explain the idea in my own words.
